To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
agouti signal peptide inhibits the production of eumorphaeomelanin in melan‐a murinie melanocytes in vitro.

agouti signal peptide, a naturally occurring inhibitor of melanin synthesis in mammals, acts in vitro to inhibit the production of eumorpha melanin by melanocytes, and that this inhibition can be reversed by the addition of melanocyte stimulating hormone.

the melanocyte‐inhibiting peptide ASP can induce melanocyte function in culture that resembles pheomelanocyte function in vivo, and that the effects of this peptide are not mediated solely through inhibition of MSH action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and biochemical mechanisms that regulate the synthesis of eumelanins and pheomelanins in mammalian skin.
the molecular mechanisms that control the switch from eumelanogenesis to pheomelanogenis, and the identification of novel factors involved in this process.
the physiological mechanisms that determine the color of mammalian hair, skin, and eyes, and with the genetic factors that cause aberrations in these traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ASP is a potent modulator of eumelanogenic function in melanocytes, and that the effects of the protein are mediated by multiple pathways.
ASP is a potent inhibitor of eumelanogenic activity in vitro, and that this inhibition can be explained in part by the down‐regulation of tyrosinase expression.

melanocytes are capable of being switched from the production of eumorphaomelanin by the presence of either ASP or α‐MSH, respectively, and that these effects are not mediated solely through the inhibition of α‐MSH binding to its receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of α‐MSH on eumelanogenesis are not simply due to the inhibition of ASP.

the melanocyte‐stimulating hormones (MSHs) are the primary regulators of eumelanogenesis, and agouti protein (ASP) is the primary regulator of pheomelagenesis, and that both MSHs and ASP act on the melanocyte through a common receptor, but that the intracellular signal transduction pathways that are activated by these two ligands are different.

the melanocyte‐stimulating hormones α‐MSH, and the related peptides, and ASP have been found to be potent stimulators and inhibitors of melanin production in melanocytes in culture, and the effects of these peptides are mediated at least in part by the melanocortin receptor 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ASP is capable of inhibiting melanogenesis in melanocytes.
agouti signal peptide (ASP) is a potent inhibitor of melanogenesis.
the effects of the ASP on melanocytes in vitro can be used to study the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of the agouti proteins on the switch between eumelanin and pheomelanogeneses.
